PR: one PR per batch into tp-run/mongodb-20260915T045208Z. It must pass `make tp-smoke`. Work through .agents/skills/tp-pre-pr-self-check/SKILL.md before opening it. State unverified paths first in the PR body. Do not edit .migration/. Do not merge your own PR.

---

Customers. The widest unit: CUSTOMER_MASTER has 155 columns and 25,000 rows, CUSTOMER_MASTER_HIST has 158 and is empty.

What this unit owns that the others do not:
- 80 columns (FLAG_01..20, UDF_01..40, UDF_AMT_01..10, UDF_DT_01..10) are dropped. Profiling found 0 non-null values across all 25,000 rows. They are listed in the spec under dropped_columns; if you find a non-null one, stop and report it.
- CUST_NAME_UPPER is dropped and replaced by a collation {locale: en, strength: 2} index on name.
- Positional columns collapse into arrays: addresses[] (physical then mailing, lines[] in column order), phones[] ({number, kind} per non-null phone, kind decoded through CODES PHONE_TYPE), emails[]. See composed_fields in the spec.
- ENTITY_ATTR_VALUE (8,333 rows, all entity_type CUSTOMER) embeds as customers.attributes[] - an ARRAY of {name, value}, not a map. 187 (entity, attr_name) pairs repeat, so a map would silently lose data.
- 50 SIGNUP_DT values do not parse as DD-MON-YY: dates.signupAt becomes null and the raw string goes to legacy.signupDtRaw. 31 RELATED_ACCT_IDS are malformed: relatedAccountIds becomes [] and the raw string goes to legacy.relatedAcctIdsRaw. These two sets are 50 and 31 exactly.
- 473 customers have status_cd 99, which has no CODES row. They are kept, decoded the way PKG_OW_UTIL.f_code_desc does it: UNKNOWN(99).
- segment, region, territory, channel, rateClass stay integers: no CODES rows exist for them. territory, channel and rateClass are null on every row.

EXPECTED COUNTS: customers 25,000; sum of customers.attributes[] 8,333; customer_history 0 (trigger-fed, empty - that is the correct result).

BRANCH AND PR: base your work on tp-run/mongodb-20260915T045208Z (the run branch), open exactly one PR for this batch into that branch, and run `make tp-smoke` before you open it.

REUSE WAVE 0: wave 0 already landed on the run branch. Use migrations/mongodb/common/ow_mongo.py rather than writing your own helpers - it has the read-only Oracle cursor (SELECT/WITH only, enforced in code), the target-database allowlist, the CODES decode including the UNKNOWN(n) fallback, Y/N to boolean, DD-MON-YY parsing that follows Oracle's YY century rule (31-DEC-99 is 2099, verified against the database), CSV split with a malformed flag, and Decimal128 money. Put your loader under migrations/mongodb/<unit>/.

THREE THINGS WAVE 0 LEARNED THE HARD WAY:
1. Your loader must converge on the source key set on a re-run, not just upsert: delete target documents whose source row is gone. See migrations/mongodb/reference/verify_idempotent.py for the proof shape (hash, reload, hash, compare).
2. The harness grades every collection in the spec it is handed, so slice the spec for your unit first: python migrations/mongodb/common/unit_spec.py <unit> .migration/recon/<unit>/mapping.json.
3. Passing a ledger path (.migration/02_tolerances.json and friends) as a command argument is blocked by the repo guard. Copy those inputs into .migration/recon/<unit>/inputs/ and point the harness at the copies. Do not pass --allowed-targets-file at all; the harness defaults to the right path.

EVIDENCE: fixture run first, then exactly one live run. Write a *.recon.json artifact with "kind": "recon-report" that lists counts recomputed from Atlas, the idempotency proof, the anomaly set, and every unverified path. Note that the harness has no rule for yn_to_bool, csv_split_trim or parse_date_string and cannot compare an integer code against its decoded string: grade those with tier 4 recorded operations (source_sql plus target_pipeline per operation) and say so in the report. Do not patch the harness.

STANDING UP THE SOURCE ON YOUR VM: the Oracle container named above runs on the parent's VM, not yours. Bring up your own deterministic copy of the same data: `make oracle-billing-up` (host port 52521; the first image pull is slow, never tear the container down to restart it) then `make oracle-billing-seed NS=demo` (seed 714559852 is derived from the namespace, so your copy is byte-identical to the parent's, and the run is safe to repeat). There is no sqlplus on the host: run ad-hoc queries through `docker exec -i otterworks-oracle-billing-oracle-billing-1 bash -c "sqlplus -s ow_billing/ow_billing@localhost:1521/FREEPDB1"` using the container's internal port 1521. Export ORACLE_BILLING_URI=ow_billing/ow_billing/localhost:52521/FREEPDB1 for the loader. Recon against this copy is run_mode fixture; the live run is the one that reads the same seeded estate under the source concurrency cap and it is the only one that carries merge authority. One gotcha the census hit: TENANTS holds 9 static baseline rows plus 60 named demo::tenant-*, so a raw count is 69.

TWO MORE THINGS WAVE 0 LEARNED IN REVIEW:
4. "kind": "recon-report" binds your artifact to docs/tech-partnerships/contracts/schema/recon-report.schema.json, which needs namespace, generated_at, run_mode, a flat checks array, values_recomputed_from_target, idempotency_rerun, planted_anomaly_detections and unverified_paths. Build it with migrations/mongodb/common/recon_report.py (it converts the harness result files into that shape) and prove it with `python scripts/tp_validate.py recon .migration/recon/<unit>/<unit>.recon.json` before you open the PR. Your unit's planted_anomaly_detections must compare the budget as a set: for the customers unit that is 50 unparseable SIGNUP_DT values and 31 malformed RELATED_ACCT_IDS lists, for the invoices unit 37 orphaned INVOICE_LINE rows, and for the other two an empty expected set.
5. Read the source in one snapshot. oracle_connect() now opens a read-only transaction so every query in a load sees one committed state; keep one connection for the whole load rather than reconnecting per table, or a parent will be copied from a later moment than its children.

---

Invoices. Two estates land in one collection, separated by the source field.

- source: "conversion" from INVOICE_HEADER (18,750 rows) with INVOICE_LINE embedded as lines[] (150,000 rows, average 8 per header, maximum 23).
- source: "billing" from INVOICES (3 rows) with INVOICE_LINES as lines[] and DUNNING_ATTEMPTS as dunning[].
- The two key spaces do not overlap (checked: 0 collisions), so _id stays the source UUID for both.
- Conversion rows carry a total only. Do not write totals.subtotal or totals.tax for them - omit the fields. Zeros would be invented data.
- CUST_NO and CUST_NAME are copied onto every INVOICE_LINE row in the source. Lift them to customer.custNo and customer.name on the header once; they are identical across a header's lines.
- 37 INVOICE_LINE rows have no matching header. They go to invoice_lines_orphaned with their dangling invoiceId kept as-is. Do not invent a header and do not drop them. The count must be exactly 37.
- lines[].type stays an integer: there is no CODES type for invoice line types, and the RPT-114 month-end report decodes it with a hard-coded DECODE.

EXPECTED COUNTS: invoices 18,753; sum of invoices.lines[] 149,965; invoice_lines_orphaned 37; sum of invoices.dunning[] 1.
